{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Deerskin / HDI Site Development, Hosting and Marketing Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (for the Company / Customer) 
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2 — 19 findings, 12 requiring action

---

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The document is commercially coherent on the revenue-share bargain but is materially incomplete on risk allocation: it contains **no indemnification, no limitation of liability, no IP ownership provision, no performance warranty, no post-termination transition or data-return mechanic, and no insurance covenant**. Because HDI designs, develops and hosts the Site and holds our Content, order/export files and user information, these gaps leave us with unallocated and uncapped exposure for IP infringement, data incidents and service failure, and with no contractual route to recover our own customer and order data on exit.

The second theme is asymmetry in the exit and restraint terms. Section 4.2(a) imposes a liquidated Termination Payment on the Company alone (50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000), which on our fee basis (30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month under Section 3.1) can exceed a full year of fees and is not disapplied where we terminate for HDI's default. Section 6.1 locks us into an open-ended exclusivity and non-compete against an auto-renewing one-year term, with no release for HDI performance failure. Section 4.1's 90-day non-renewal window and Section 3.4's uncapped inspection right are lesser but real deviations.

Good news worth preserving: governing law (New York, Section 10.5) is at our preferred position; there is **no** MFN, **no** minimum purchase or volume commitment, **no** non-solicit binding us, no change-of-control trigger, no restriction on our assignment, and no disclaimer of implied warranties. HDI's reciprocal two-year non-compete (Section 6.3) benefits us and we leave it untouched.

Of the 12 action items, 3 are critical, 4 are high, 4 are medium and 1 is low. Six of these are proposed at the playbook fallback rather than the preferred position, reflecting the branded-site build-out bargain.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / proposed action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 (insert as § 9(c)) | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless anywhere; walk-away territory. Add HDI indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, plus a narrow Company indemnity limited to Company-supplied Content/Marks. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 1.4 (insert as § 5.5) | No ownership clause; Section 8 protects but does not allocate, and § 5.2 gives only artistic/editorial control. Insert: Company retains Content, Marks and customer/order data; HDI assigns Site/deliverables with licence-back of its pre-existing platform; no joint ownership. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 (insert as § 10.9) | No cap, exclusion or aggregate-liability language. Add mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; uncapped carve-outs (confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement); confirm §§ 3 and 4.2 payments are not "damages". |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 (§ 10.3) | § 10.3 is successors/no-third-party-beneficiary only; HDI may assign to a competitor with no notice or consent. Add affiliate/successor right for us, confirmation our change of control gives HDI no termination or re-pricing right, and a consent/no-competitor gate on HDI assignment. Fallback: mutual successor assignment on notice with reasonable-consent standard. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 (§ 6.1) | Open-ended exclusivity against an auto-renewing term, exit only via the § 4.2(a) Termination Payment, no performance-based release. Narrow to Deerskin Products, cap at 12 months from the Effective Date, automatic release on HDI launch or performance failure (fallback proposed, not deletion). |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 (§ 4.2(a)) | Company-payable exit formula can exceed a year of fees and the value of the remaining term, and is not disapplied for HDI default. Cap at three months' fees and disapply where we terminate for HDI's breach. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 (§ 6.1) | Scope reaches "substantially similar" products and an open-ended third-party class; no internal-development or acquisition carve-out; term-only but indefinitely renewing. Narrow to Deerskin Products, cap at 12 months, add internal-development/acquisition carve-out. |
| 8 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 1.4 (§§ 4.1, 4.2(a)) | 90-day mutual notice mechanics sit at the fallback and are not redlined; the Company-only Termination Payment is the failure. Cap at three months' § 3.1 fees and disapply for HDI breach or the § 1.6 launch-failure right. |
| 9 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 (§ 3.4) | Clause already exceeds playbook on notice, timing, cost and system access, but has no frequency limit (unlimited audits are walk-away territory). Add a once-per-twelve-month cap. Use of HDI's General Manager rather than an independent auditor is noted, not redlined. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 5.4 (§ 10.5) | New York law, our preferred position; no arbitration and no other venue anywhere. Absence of an express exclusive-jurisdiction reference to New York County courts is optional cleanup only. |
| 11 | Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 | Grant names "the Company" only, with no extension to affiliates or contractors and no mechanism to add them. Extend § 1.4 access/use rights to affiliates and contractors and confirm they are not revocable at will. Successor transfer is covered by § 10.3. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 1.4 (§ 3) | No MFN or best-terms mechanic in either direction; flat 30% share of Net Sales above a monthly threshold. Preferred position met; no redline. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 1.4 (§ 3) | Pure revenue share on actual Net Sales above $11,000/month; no minimum, take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or usage cap; one-year auto-renewing term. Preferred position met. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 5.4 | No solicit/hire/inducement covenant anywhere; § 6.3's two-year restraint binds HDI, not us. Preferred position met. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 1.4 (§ 4.1) | One-year renewal term matches preferred, but the 90-day non-renewal window exceeds the 60-day fallback ceiling. Shorten to 30 days (60 days acceptable). No reminder mechanic and no repricing language — noted only. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 (insert as § 4.3) | § 4 covers only notice, Termination Date and Termination Payment; no migration, export, return or deletion obligation, and § 10.7 survival does not reach it. Insert up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of Content and data (including Site credentials) in machine-readable form within 30 days, then certified deletion. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.4 (§ 9) | § 9 covers corporate reps plus the Globix acknowledgement only; no workmanlike-services, conformance, legal-compliance or malicious-code warranty and no remedy. Add as new § 9(c) with repair/re-perform/refund remedy (12 months preferred; 90-day fallback available). No implied-warranty disclaimer exists. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 (insert as § 10.9) | No insurance covenant; HDI hosts the Site and processes our Content and user information, so an uninsured vendor is walk-away territory. Insert CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request. Fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

---

## Walk-away items

The following findings fall into, or sit immediately adjacent to, walk-away territory under the playbook and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **No vendor indemnity (INDEMN, § 5.4 / § 9).** The complete absence of any indemnity, defence or hold-harmless obligation — leaving us with no IP indemnity for a Site HDI develops and hosts, and no coverage for HDI's breach of law, data incidents or gross negligence/wilful misconduct — is expressly walk-away territory.
2. **No insurance (INSURANCE, § 5.4 / § 10).** Leaving a hosting vendor that processes our Content and user information uninsured is walk-away territory under the rule.
3. **Unlimited HDI inspection right (AUDIT, § 3.4).** The clause is otherwise favourable, but unlimited audit frequency is walk-away territory; the once-per-twelve-month cap is the minimum acceptable outcome.
4. **Company-only exclusivity with no performance release (EXCLUSIVITY, § 6.1).** Open-ended lock-in surviving HDI's failure to keep the Site operational is close to walk-away territory; the 12-month cap plus automatic release on performance failure is our floor.

Related, and to be resolved together: the **missing limitation of liability (§ 10.9 proposed)** leaves every one of the above exposures uncapped, so items 1–3 should be negotiated as a package with the LOL insertion.

---

## Next steps

1. **Send the redline with a covering note framing the four insertions as a package** — indemnity (§ 9(c)), limitation of liability (§ 10.9), IP ownership (§ 5.5) and insurance (§ 10.9) — on the basis that HDI builds, hosts and holds the data, so risk allocation cannot be left silent.
2. **Open the exit economics as a single negotiation.** LD and T4C both turn on § 4.2(a); we ask for the same fix once — cap the Termination Payment at three months' § 3.1 fees and disapply it where we terminate for HDI's breach or under the § 1.6 launch-failure right. We should be prepared to trade here, as this is HDI's principal protection for its build-out investment.
3. **Bundle the restraint asks.** EXCLUSIVITY and NONCOMPETE are both § 6.1: narrow to Deerskin Products, cap at 12 months, add the internal-development/acquisition carve-out and automatic release on HDI performance failure. We confirm we are not touching HDI's reciprocal § 6.3 covenant, which favours us — worth saying so expressly.
4. **Table the low-friction items for quick agreement:** the § 3.4 once-a-year audit cap, the § 4.1 notice window (30 days preferred, 60 acceptable), the § 1.4 affiliate/contractor extension, and the new § 4.3 transition and data-return mechanic.
5. **Confirm internally before sending:** (a) the Net Sales history needed to size the § 4.2(a) exposure against three months' fees; (b) whether operations require affiliate or contractor access to the § 1.4 hosting tools, and by whom; (c) the transition window we actually need (we have proposed six months at HDI's then-current rates); and (d) that the proposed insurance limits match our current vendor standard.
6. **Optional cleanup only, at our discretion:** add an express exclusive-jurisdiction reference to the state and federal courts in New York County to § 10.5. Governing law is already at our preferred position, so we would not spend leverage here.

We have not proposed changes to any provision that benefits us, and we have not flagged the compliant items (GOVLAW, MFN, MINCOMMIT, NOSOLICIT) other than to record that they meet the playbook."}
